subject: ophthalmology
title: Optics and errors of refraction: core principles for NEET-PG and INI-CET

steps.tx: A newborn eye is normally **hypermetropic** by about +2 to +3 D because the eyeball is short, around 17 mm. Most children become emmetropic by about 5 to 7 years as the eye grows. The axial length in adults is near 24 mm. Eyes longer than this tend towards **myopia** and shorter eyes towards **hypermetropia**.
steps.say: A newborn eye is normally hypermetropic by about plus two to plus three dioptres because the eyeball is short, around 17 millimetres. Most children become emmetropic by about 5 to 7 years as the eye grows. The axial length in adults is near 24 millimetres. Eyes longer than this tend towards myopia and shorter eyes towards hypermetropia.

steps.tx: **Accommodation** is the eye's ability to increase its power for near objects, mainly by the lens becoming more convex. It involves ciliary muscle contraction, constriction of the pupil and an increase in anterior lens curvature. Pupil **dilatation** is not part of accommodation. With age the amplitude falls, and **presbyopia** begins near 40 to 45 years because the lens loses elasticity.

steps.tx: In **hypermetropia**, a patient may use accommodation to see clearly, and this leads to convergence and sometimes esotropia. In **myopia**, near work is easy, so convergence is less used and the eye tends to diverge. Pseudomyopia is a transient myopic shift from ciliary spasm and is confirmed by cycloplegic refraction. Retinoscopy with neutralisation is the **objective** test of refraction.

rows: Emmetropia or hypermetropia, or myopia under 1 D

steps.tx: **Pathological myopia** is greater than -6 D, starts in childhood and is linked to rapid axial growth. Its complications include **retinal detachment**, complicated cataract, vitreous and choroidal haemorrhage. Fundus signs include myopic crescents, Fuchs spots and posterior staphyloma. Treatment of ordinary myopia uses concave lenses, while presbyopia is corrected with convex near lenses.
